stem: Department A of a firm has 40 employees with mean salary Rs 30,000 and standard deviation Rs 6,000. Department B has 60 employees with mean salary Rs 40,000 and standard deviation Rs 8,000. Find the combined standard deviation of all 100 employees.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student computes SD as simple average (6+8)/2 = 7, using arithmetic mean of the two SDs instead of the combined variance formula.
Student ignores the between-group term (d1^2 and d2^2): combined variance = (40*36+60*64)/100 = 5280/100 = 52.8, SD = sqrt(52.8) = 7.265.
Student computes sqrt((var1+var2)/2) = sqrt((36+64)/2) = sqrt(50) = 7.071, using the simple average of the variances.

explanation: The combined variance formula accounts for both within-group variance and between-group variance (the squared difference between each group mean and the combined mean).

explanation_sections.punchline: The critical between-group term n1*d1^2 + n2*d2^2 always increases the combined variance above the weighted average of the individual variances.
explanation_sections.lesson: Simply averaging the SDs or variances ignores the between-group spread; the combined SD is always at least as large as the larger individual SD when the means differ.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. The main computation is the four-product sum; keep track of d1^2=36 and d2^2=16 carefully.
